text:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert -> continuous-batcher: kv-prefetch spin + paging causing GPU NMI and container restarts in us-west-2a. Paging high, tail latency and 5xxs rising. Paging on nodes: i-0a*, i-0b*. Pinging @sofia for oncall

sofia (oncall): ack. seeing a spike in OOM/restart events for the continuous-batcher pods in gpu-pool-usw2a. containers keep restarting every ~20-40s. metrics: batch_queue_len -> growth, kvcache.prefetch_bytes -> steady climb.

sofia (oncall): quick tl;dr from logs: multiple `NVRM: Xid 13` and `GPU reset` followed by `oom-killer` in container. also kernel shows pagefault storms.

raj (eng-runtime): copying relevant dmesg snippet, looks like classic GPU page thrash -> NMI reset pattern:

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID: 20480 ...
[ 1234.568000] GPU crash dump:
[ 1234.568100] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568200] oom_reaper: reaped process 20480 (batcher-worker)
[ 1234.569000] pagefault: excessive PFN cache miss, prefetch backlog growing
```

raj (eng-runtime): root cause hypothesis: prefetcher + large continuous batches are driving KV cache growth; when kvcache exceeds device mem, runtime triggers paged GPU allocations causing thrash and then CUDA NMI/resets.

tim-sre: confirming node-level symptoms -> host vmstat shows high `pgfault` and `pgscan` around the same time. also see `IB` link flaps on one host, maybe exacerbating memory pressure.

sofia (oncall): immediate mitigation path I propose (fast, reversible):
- scale down `batcher.max_batch_tokens` to 256 in cluster config (reduces working set)
- disable `kvcache.prefetch` on affected pool: `PATCH /v1/cluster/pools/gpu-pool-usw2a {"kvcache": {"prefetch": false}}`
- cordon + drain the most-erroring node (i-0b*) to stop repeated GPU resets on that host
- spin up 2 additional gpu nodes as buffer (auto-scale failing), or fallback to smaller model CPU pool for critical requests

karen (sre-lead): +1 to those, I'll own the handoff. if we don't see recovery in 10m, we should force a canary rollback to the previous model runtime (quantized 4-bit) and re-enable strict eviction.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started -> rolling restart of continuous-batcher with `max_batch_tokens=256` and `kvcache.prefetch=false` applied to canary subset (pods continuous-batcher-canary-*)

sofia (oncall): customer impact: support feed shows ~3 customers experiencing elevated 5xx (error: `model-unavailable` and `gpu-reset`), overall 5xx rate in us-west-2a ~6.8% over last 5m, tail latency hitting 14-18s. Not a global outage but user-facing degradation. support has been notified.

customer-ops: posted pro-active note to affected accounts: "We've identified transient GPU instability causing elevated errors; mitigation underway; ETA 15-30m."

raj (eng-runtime): also pushed a runtime toggle to enable `kvcache.strict_eviction=true` which will aggressively evict cold prefixes once canary restart completes. command run: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://internal-api/cluster/config -d '{"kvcache": {"strict_eviction": true}}'`

mike-ml: flagging that dropping `max_batch_tokens` could reduce throughput and increase per-request cost; but OK for stability. if we need longer term, we should consider limiting prefetch depth per-request and add prefetch backpressure.

sofia (oncall): canary is stabilizing, canary pods show no further GPU resets for 2 cycles. continuing rollout to remaining pods with same config.

ops-bot: node i-0b* marked UNHEALTHY by autoscaler; cordoned and drained by sofia. replacing with new instance.

karen (sre-lead): handoff -> I'm taking lead for the next 2h. sofia, document any lingering customers and assign post-incident follow-up to runtime team for a proper root-cause. immediate owner: raj.

sofia (oncall): handoff ack. notes left in incident board: `kvcache prefetch + continuous batch growth -> pgfault -> CUDA NMI -> container crash`. follow-up actions assigned:
- runtime: add prefetch backpressure + per-pool mem limit (assigned to raj)
- infra: improve autoscaler aggressiveness for gpu pool and node health detection (assigned to tim-sre)
- product/ML: evaluate batching defaults and model memory requirements (assigned to mike-ml)

karen (sre-lead): customers clear? support confirm?

customer-ops: affected accounts reporting improved latency and reduced 5xx after rollout. closing customer notices pending final RCA.

karen (sre-lead): marking SEV2 mitigated. will keep this open for RCA and follow-ups. leaving handback timestamp and notes. thanks everyone for quick reactions :thumbsup:

sofia (oncall): leaving channel, handed to karen. pairing notes pasted into incident ticket.

incident-bot: incident update -> status: mitigated, severity: SEV2 -> owner: karen (sre-lead).
